svg.title: The learning loop: uncertain detections become questions; human answers refit the models; held-out gates decide what the model may settle on its own
svg.text: 1 · Analysis of a video
every Pokémon gets a posterior:
fast move p · Shadow p · form p
every battle: result + source
saved evidence: HP series, aura, hits
2 · Questions, only if unsure
fast move p < .85 · Shadow .15–.85
form unsettled · result not read
ordered by impact: uncertainty ×
species frequency ÷ answers already
questions.js · validation-policy.js
3 · A person answers
watches the clip at that moment
Yes / No / move / “Not sure” / Skip
answers are labels; model guesses
never become labels
Validate tab · feedback.json
4 · Refit from saved evidence (after 8 useful answers)
species priors (fast moves, Shadow rates, forms)
evidence settings every 24 labels (noise, timing, energy)
Shadow classifier weights (L2 logistic regression)
no video is decoded; a refit of 37 videos takes seconds
feedback.py · learning-loop.cjs · refit.cjs · movefit-fit.cjs
5 · Held out by video, then gates
each video is scored with priors learned from the others
pick the lowest confidence at which held-out answers were
≥ 95% right, over ≥ 30 answers from ≥ 5 videos,
Wilson lower bound ≥ .90 (Shadow: ≥ 25 calls, ≥ .80)
fast moves: p ≥ .90 (102/103) · forms: not yet · Shadow: by direction
6 · Every saved result is re-derived
confident items are settled by the model (reversible,
audited as “model resolved”); the rest stay open
result rules promote/demote at ≥ 95% on ≥ 30 answers
human answers always win over any model output
metrics-history.json → Model performance view
Why this design
labels are scarce and expensive (a person per answer),
so the model must ask the most informative questions,
must never train on its own guesses, and must prove
on unseen videos that it is right before it stops asking.
audit spot checks (2 per video) keep measuring confident calls
dashed: the next analysis, and every saved one, uses the refitted priors and settings
